features.source_name: Univ. of Illinois IPM, Corn Flea Beetle Insect Fact Sheet (UIUC-CFB)

features.description: Leaf streaks on dent corn usually appear after tasseling.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: If the mean daily temperature in December–February is above freezing, vectors survive and severe disease is possible. Below −3 °C, survival is unlikely and severe disease is unlikely.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: Non-motile, non-spore-forming, **Gram-negative rods**, 0.4–0.7 × 0.9–2.0 µm, occurring singly or in short chains.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: On nutrient-glucose agar, colonies are cream-yellow, lemon-yellow or orange-yellow, and flat, raised or convex.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: EPPO diagnostic protocol **PM 7/60(2)** covers isolation, immunofluorescence (IF), ELISA, molecular tests (conventional and real-time PCR, barcoding) and fatty acid analysis. The USA recommends ELISA-based testing of maize seed lots. The PM 7/60 text itself could not be opened.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: Adults: small, shiny black, about 1/16 inch (≈1.6 mm, converted), with thick hind legs, good jumpers. Larvae: small, white and not very active. Mature larvae are 1/6 inch (≈4.2 mm, converted), with only the prothorax and last abdominal segment slightly darker.
features.source_name: Univ. of Illinois IPM, Corn Flea Beetle Insect Fact Sheet (UIUC-CFB)

features.description: Scrapes the upper and lower leaf epidermis, leaving **scratches usually parallel to the veins (windowpane)**. Does not chew through the leaf. Heavily fed leaves look white or silvery. Leaves can be covered with feeding scars when new adults emerge in June and August.
features.source_name: Univ. of Illinois IPM, Corn Flea Beetle Insect Fact Sheet (UIUC-CFB)

features.description: Overwinters as adults in soil and debris along fencerows, roadsides and woodland edges. Becomes active at 65–70 °F (≈18–21 °C, converted). One generation takes about a month, with first-generation adults in June and second-generation adults in early August. A third generation may occur in southern Illinois. Seen first at field edges.
features.source_name: Univ. of Illinois IPM, Corn Flea Beetle Insect Fact Sheet (UIUC-CFB)

features.description: The main US vector is *C. pulicaria*. Adults overwinter and carry the bacteria in the gut for life. They can travel long distances on air currents. Vector morphology is not described.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: Goss's wilt can look very similar. *Acidovorax avenae*: long narrow streaks with reddish-brown margins, leaf shredding. *Burkholderia andropogonis*: long narrow parallel olive-green to yellow water-soaked lesions. Northern corn leaf blight: large spindle-shaped gray-green to tan spots. Southern corn leaf blight and *C. carbonum*: well-defined tan to brown spots.
features.source_name: EPPO Global Database, *Pantoea stewartii* subsp. *stewartii* datasheet (EPPO-ERWIST)

features.description: Both Goss's and Stewart's diseases cause seedling blight and long lesions with wavy margins between veins. The distinguishing feature is the dark green to black freckles of Goss's. Stewart's has been rarely recorded since the early 2000s.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)
features.location_in_source: Diseases and Other Conditions with Similar Symptoms > Stewart's

source_conflicts: Leaf lesion color: the starting color is 'pale green to yellow' in both EPPO and CPN, and the final color is 'straw-colored/brown' in EPPO and 'brown' in CPN. Water-soaked margins appear only in UIUC (sweet corn seedlings) and the CPN photo description.
Two phases: EPPO and UIUC separate the wilt phase (sweet corn, seedlings) and leaf blight phase (dent corn, after tasseling), but CPN-Stewart (2026 edition) does not describe them separately.
Bacterial exudate: EPPO 'masses of yellow bacterial slime', CPN 'pale yellow droplets'.
Vector morphology was confirmed in only one source, UIUC (about 1/16 in, shiny black). EPPO and CPN do not describe it.
Recent frequency: CPN-Goss says it has been rarely recorded since the early 2000s, while EPPO keeps the USA as 'Present, widespread' (different indicators).
diseases.photo_visible: Pale green to yellow wavy-margined streaks starting from flea beetle feeding scratches, wilting of sweet corn seedlings, feeding scars parallel to the veins (windowpane), yellow bacterial slime at cut surfaces.
diseases.lab_required: Bacterial streaming from vascular bundles (microscopy ×100), Gram-negative rods and yellowish colonies (culture), IF, ELISA and PCR (EPPO PM 7/60), definitive separation from Goss's wilt.

diseases.name_en: Goss's bacterial wilt and leaf blight
diseases.intro: No Korean source confirmed. The EPPO distribution table has no entry for Korea or Asia (this does not confirm absence). Bacterial cell size and colony color could not be confirmed from primary sources.

features.description: Korean source: Unconfirmed. The EPPO distribution table has no entry for Korea or Asia. This does not confirm absence. The EPPO web datasheet showed only Identity and distribution; the symptom and morphology sections could not be viewed.
features.source_name: EPPO CORBNE

features.description: Young lesions are light green water-soaked streaks with gray-green margins. When mature they become long tan to gray-brown lesions with irregular or wavy margins parallel to the veins. They often start at the leaf tip or at hail or sandblasting wounds. When lesions merge, more than 60% of the leaf area can die.
features.short_quote: "streaks of light green tissue with water-soaking"
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Long, large tan lesions form in the middle or along the margin of the leaf. Margins may look water-soaked.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Within lesions there are scattered, discontinuous dark green to black water-soaked spots (freckles). They look translucent against the light and are diagnostic of Goss's.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: The black spots (freckles) within lesions can be large and **do not rub off**. They are mainly at lesion margins but may be scattered throughout the lesion.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Freckles form near the margins of expanding lesions.
features.source_name: Univ. of Nebraska–Lincoln CropWatch, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight (UNL-Goss)

features.description: Under humid conditions small orange droplets of bacterial exudate form on lesions. Dried exudate shines like dried varnish.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Exudate is visible on lesion surfaces in the early morning or after rain. Dried exudate is glossy, especially in direct sunlight.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Bacteria produce exudate on the leaf surface, which shines like varnish when dry.
features.source_name: Univ. of Nebraska–Lincoln CropWatch, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight (UNL-Goss)

features.description: Bacteria streaming from lesion sections (bacterial streaming) can be seen under the microscope.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Xylem discoloration or slimy stalk rot develops, leading through wilting to death. Figure 6 shows 'discolored stalk pith'. The discoloration color is not described.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Stalk vascular bundles **discolor orange to brown** because the bacteria move within the xylem.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: As bacteria infect and move through the vascular bundles, the xylem discolors, and eventually the plant wilts and dies of slimy stalk rot. Color is not described.
features.source_name: Univ. of Nebraska–Lincoln CropWatch, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight (UNL-Goss)

features.description: Plants with the wilt phase show drought-stress symptoms and wilt or die early.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Plants infected late wilt as if from drought, and weakened stalks lodge easily.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Infection can occur at any growth stage. Infection before V6 usually becomes systemic, causing death and stand loss, and systemic wilt is often first seen at V2–V6. Infection after V6 becomes leaf blight. Symptoms are most distinct and severe after silking (R1). Infection during the vegetative stage can reduce yield by more than 50%.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Enters any part of the plant through hail or strong-wind wounds and spreads by windblown rain. It can also enter through insect feeding wounds, but insects do not transmit it. Hot, dry weather slows progression, making it hard to distinguish from drought.
features.short_quote: "insects are not known to transmit the bacteria"
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Seed-to-seedling transmission is low at about 2%, but infected seed can introduce the disease to new areas.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Transmitted by seed, but seedling transmission is low so it is not regarded as a main source of infection. Infected residue on the soil surface is the main inoculum.
features.source_name: Univ. of Nebraska–Lincoln CropWatch, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight (UNL-Goss)

features.description: A **Gram-positive bacterium** (one of the few plant diseases caused by Gram-positive bacteria). Cell size and colony color are not given in this source.
features.source_name: Univ. of Nebraska–Lincoln CropWatch, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight (UNL-Goss)

features.description: For confirmation, send samples for diagnostic lab testing including microscopy, isolation and serological tests.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

features.description: Northern corn leaf blight lesions are canoe- or cigar-shaped, 1–4 inches (≈2.5–10 cm, converted) long and 1/2–1 inch wide. Early margins are gray-green, and mature lesions are tan with dark sporulation. Margins are even, with no freckles or streaming. On some hybrids margin discoloration can look like freckles.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: *X. vasicola* pv. *vasculorum*: narrower tan to yellow lesions than Goss's, from under 1 inch to several inches long, bright yellow against the light. No freckles; streaming can occur in both diseases.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus deficiencies lack water-soaked freckles, glossy exudate and streaming. Drought and leaf scorch usually progress inward from the leaf margin, are more uniform in color, and lack those three features.
features.source_name: Crop Protection Network, An Overview of Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Blight (CPN-Goss)

features.description: Leaf blight is easily confused with drought or chemical leaf scorch in dry weather. It can also be misdiagnosed as nutrient deficiency, chemical injury, Stewart's disease or northern corn leaf blight.
features.source_name: Wise, Ruhl, Creswell, Goss's Bacterial Wilt and Leaf Blight, Purdue Ext. BP-81-W (2010-05) (Purdue-BP81)

source_conflicts: Freckle location: CPN 'scattered within lesions', UNL 'near the margins of expanding lesions', Purdue 'mainly at margins but also throughout the lesion'.
Freckle color: CPN 'dark green to black', Purdue 'black spots'.
Only Purdue states the color of vascular discoloration ('orange to brown'); CPN and UNL say only 'discoloration'.
Exudate color: CPN 'orange droplets' under humid conditions, while Purdue and UNL mention only 'glossy' with no color.
Seed transmission: Purdue 'about 2%', UNL 'low'.
Survival in residue: CPN 'at least 10–15 months', Purdue '10 months on the surface under dry conditions'.
Colony color is left Unconfirmed because, at search-summary level, 'apricot to orange (NBY)' and 'yellow on most media' do not agree (source PMC4658045 blocked; EPPO Alert list 404).
diseases.photo_visible: Long tan to gray-brown lesions with wavy margins, dark green to black water-soaked freckles within lesions (translucent against light, do not rub off), glossy exudate like dried varnish, orange to brown discoloration of stalk vascular bundles.
diseases.lab_required: Bacterial streaming (microscopy), Gram-positive confirmation, isolation and serological tests, definitive separation from Stewart's wilt, drought and nutrient deficiency.

diseases.intro: No Korean source confirmed. Korea is not in the Asia section of the EPPO distribution table. Below are descriptions from the US government (three CAPS editions) and original papers (Singh, Groben 2026).

features.description: Korean source: Unconfirmed. Korea is not among the Asian entries of the EPPO distribution table (Guangxi China, India, Indonesia, Nepal, Pakistan, Philippines, Thailand). Only Identity and distribution of the EPPO web datasheet could be viewed.
features.source_name: EPPO-PRSCPH

features.description: The first symptoms appear as chlorotic streaks on the first leaves as early as **9 days after sowing**.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Long chlorotic (yellow) streaks may appear on all leaves of a plant. Heavily infected cells collapse and chloroplasts are destroyed, giving a yellow color (Weston 1920).
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Distinct green and yellow streaks form on leaves, and a gray to white downy coating may grow on the leaf surface.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS datasheet *P. philippinensis* Version 2 (2021-09-29) (CAPS-Pp-2021)

features.description: Chlorosis spreads widely and white downy masses form on the leaf underside. Ear development is delayed or poor.
features.short_quote: "white downy mass on the ventral leaf surface"
features.source_name: Singh J., "Relative disease reaction of maize varieties to downy mildews over varied environments (IDMN 1969–1973)", Tropical Agriculture Research Series No. 8, pp.129–152 (JIRCAS publication; **publication year unconfirmed in the original**) (Singh-TARS8)

features.description: A gray downy coating (conidia on conidiophores) forms mainly on the leaf underside. It is visible **from the 2-leaf stage until tassels and silks emerge** and is a source of secondary spread.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Conidiophores emerge from stomata in chlorotic areas on both leaf surfaces (more on the underside, where stomata are more numerous). They also emerge from leaf sheaths, the tassel axis, glumes and husks.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Sporulation begins around midnight and continues until the surface dries. After 1–2 hours of exposure to sunlight, wind or low humidity, conidia shrivel. Conidia are sparse the morning after the first symptoms and abundant after systemic symptoms.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Grayish-white down is present on chlorotic areas but may dry from sunlight or low humidity, leaving only 'matted patches'.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Small Grains manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (Table 1, citing White 1999) (CAPS-Pp-SG)

features.description: From the seedling, yellow streaks enlarge on successively higher leaves (a scouting point).
features.short_quote: "larger and larger yellow streaks on succeeding leaves"
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Small Grains manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (Table 1, citing White 1999) (CAPS-Pp-SG)

features.description: Mycelium spreads between mesophyll cells, moves down the leaf sheath, passes through the stalk and establishes in the growing point. Once the meristem is invaded, chlorotic streaks soon form and spores are produced there. The fungus is present only in chlorotic, not green, areas.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: As plants grow, leaves become narrow, abnormally upright and look dry.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: At maturity tassels become malformed with reduced pollen, ear formation stops, and seed may be sterile. Early infection causes stunting or death.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn); USDA CAPS datasheet *P. philippinensis* Version 2 (2021-09-29) (CAPS-Pp-2021)

features.description: Seeds show no external symptoms. Mycelium is in the pericarp and also in the embryo and endosperm.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Sugarcane: the bases of young leaves turn white, and old leaves show mosaic or mottling and then turn brick-red. Stalks become thin.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS datasheet *P. philippinensis* Version 2 (2021-09-29) (CAPS-Pp-2021)

features.description: Conidia are produced at 18–23 °C and germinate at 10–35 °C. Infection is highest above 16 °C. Night temperatures of 21–26 °C are needed for conidial production, germination and infection. A water film on the leaf surface in darkness for at least 4–5 hours is required.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: An obligate biotroph that does not grow on artificial media. Hyphae are branched and slender (8 µm diameter), irregularly constricted or swollen. Conidiophores are erect, **15–26 × 150–400 µm**, emerge from stomata and **branch dichotomously 2–4 times** with stout branches. Sterigmata are ovoid to subulate, slightly curved, 10 µm long. Conidia are **17–21 × 27–39 µm**, elongate-ovoid to rounded cylindrical, hyaline, with slightly rounded tips. Haustoria are simple vesicular to digitate, 8 × 2 µm.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Oospores are rare and not produced in maize tissue. When produced they are globose, smooth-walled, about 22 µm in diameter, germinating by a lateral germ tube.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Table 1 (White 1999): ***P. philippinensis*** conidiophores 150–400 µm, swollen and abruptly widening, 2–4 dichotomous branchings, ephemeral; conidia 17–21 × 27–39 µm; oospores rare or absent, 22.6 µm. ***P. maydis*** conidiophores 150–550 µm; conidia globose to subglobose 17–23 × 27–39 µm; oospores unknown. ***P. sacchari*** conidiophores 160–170 µm, gradually widening, 2–3 branchings; conidia elliptical, oblong or conical '15-239' (apparently a misprint) × 25–41 µm; oospores yellow to yellow-brown 40–50 µm. ***P. sorghi*** conidiophores 180–300 µm, 2–3 branchings, septum near the base; conidia elliptical to nearly globose 15–26.9 × 15–28.9 µm; oospores usually brown 25–42.9 µm. All *Peronosclerospora* conidia germinate by a **germ tube**.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Small Grains manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (Table 1, citing White 1999) (CAPS-Pp-SG)

features.description: Morphological characters vary greatly with culture conditions, developmental stage and host. *Peronosclerospora* is divided by conidial shape into three groups (globose / ovoid to slightly elongate / long or slipper-shaped), but differences within groups are small.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Downy mildew fungi are distinguished only by fine morphological differences, so definitive identification is difficult. Conidiophores may exist for only a few hours, and morphology is affected by environment and host. Eleven downy mildew species in 3 genera have been reported on maize.
features.source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)

features.description: CAPS-approved method: morphological identification by conidiophore structure and size and conidial shape and size. Isozyme comparison has also been used. At the time of writing there was no species-specific PCR (only tools for related species, such as a *P. sorghi* SCAR and a *P. sacchari* DNA probe).
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)

features.description: Since other endemic downy mildews (*P. maydis*, *P. spontanea*) produce similar symptoms, field symptoms alone cannot give accurate identification. Molecular identification is needed for confirmation.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS datasheet *P. philippinensis* Version 2 (2021-09-29) (CAPS-Pp-2021)

features.description: In a 62-ortholog phylogeny, the *P. philippinensis* lectotype (BPI 187314) belongs to subgroup B2 and falls in a different clade from the *P. sacchari* lectotype. Therefore the two species are kept separate. The conspecific view based on morphology, host range and isozymes was not adopted. Host range is of little diagnostic use.
features.short_quote: "both taxa were upheld as distinct species"
features.source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)
features.location_in_source: Discussion 'P. philippinensis and P. sacchari'; Taxonomy

features.description: Maize downy mildews are caused by up to 10 species in the genera *Peronosclerospora*, *Sclerophthora* and *Sclerospora*. Other endemic downy mildews (e.g., *P. sorghi*) and physiological disorders (fertility, weather) also produce similar symptoms. MSV infection can mask downy mildew symptoms.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (CAPS-Pp-corn)
features.location_in_source: p.4 Known Vectors; p.6 Easily Confused Pests

features.description: Other downy mildews in the same table: sugarcane downy mildew (*S. sacchari*) has yellow to white streaks at the base of leaves 3–6 and increased ear number; sorghum downy mildew has pale green to cream parallel streaks and a fan of small leaves at the plant top; crazy top has chlorotic streaks weaker than Philippine downy mildew and phyllody of the tassel. Downy mildews differ only in detailed symptoms, so **species cannot be accurately identified from field symptoms alone**.
features.source_name: Singh J., "Relative disease reaction of maize varieties to downy mildews over varied environments (IDMN 1969–1973)", Tropical Agriculture Research Series No. 8, pp.129–152 (JIRCAS publication; **publication year unconfirmed in the original**) (Singh-TARS8)

source_conflicts: Taxonomy (largest difference): the CAPS 2009 lineage includes *P. sacchari* as a synonym and treats them as conspecific, the CAPS 2021 edition removes it from the synonyms, and Groben 2026 keeps them as separate species based on molecular data. The alternative name 'Java downy mildew' is also attached to different species by CAPS versus Groben and Table 1.

Diagnostic method: the CAPS 2009 edition says morphological identification is the approved method and no species-specific PCR exists, while the CAPS 2021 edition says molecular identification is needed.
Oospore size: CAPS Corn text 'about 22 µm', Table 1 '22.6 µm'.
Down color and position: CAPS 'gray, mainly leaf underside', CAPS 2021 'gray to white, leaf surface', Singh 'white, leaf underside'.
Misprint: the *P. sacchari* conidial width '15-239' in CAPS Small Grains Table 1 appears to be a misprint (other species in the same table are around 15–27 µm).
Distribution: CAPS includes Japan, DR Congo, Mauritius and South Africa, but EPPO marks South Africa and the USA as 'Absent, unreliable record' and does not list Japan.
diseases.photo_visible: Long chlorotic (yellow) streaks appearing from 9 days after sowing and enlarging on higher leaves, grayish-white down on the leaf underside in early morning, narrow upright leaves, tassel malformation.
diseases.lab_required: Conidiophores branching dichotomously 2–4 times and elongate-ovoid conidia (microscopy; figures overlap with related species), species-specific molecular identification (separation from *P. maydis*, *P. sacchari* and others), mycelium inside seed.

diseases.intro: No Korean source confirmed. Korea is not in the EPPO distribution (India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand). Everything below is an overseas description.

features.description: Korean source: Unconfirmed. Korea is not in the EPPO distribution (India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand). Only Identity and distribution of the EPPO web datasheet could be viewed.
features.source_name: EPPO-SCPHRZ

features.description: The latest name is "*Sclerophthora zeae* (formerly *S. rayssiae* var. *zeae*)", described as a US Select Agent. The publication establishing this combination is Unconfirmed.
features.source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)

features.description: Lesions form **only on leaves**. At first they are narrow chlorotic or yellow streaks like other downy mildews but only **3–7 mm** wide. Borders are distinct and delimited by veins. In some genotypes they later turn red to purple.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Narrow chlorotic or yellow streaks of variable length, bounded by veins. They later become necrotic and take on a **brown, burnt appearance**.
features.source_name: Singh J., "Relative disease reaction of maize varieties to downy mildews over varied environments (IDMN 1969–1973)", Tropical Agriculture Research Series No. 8, pp.129–152 (JIRCAS publication; **publication year unconfirmed in the original**) (Singh-TARS8)

features.description: As lesions spread laterally they become severe striping and blotching. They are noticeable first and most severe on lower leaves and look pale brown and burnt. Severely affected leaves may drop early.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Blotching before flowering suppresses grain development, giving small seed, and plants may die early. If more than 3/4 of the leaf is infected before flowering, total loss is possible, and ear formation is completely suppressed or greatly weakened.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Unlike other downy mildews, **floral or vegetative organs are not malformed and leaves do not shred**. It appears not to infect systemically.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Spores form on both lesion surfaces, appearing downy or woolly. When lesions become necrotic, sporangia disappear.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Check for down on both leaf surfaces on **cool, humid mornings**. The down usually disappears by late afternoon. Infected leaves remain intact.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Oospores and oogonia are scattered abundantly in the mesophyll of necrotic tissue or below stomata. They are not in the vascular bundles.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Young plants are most susceptible, and susceptibility declines with age. Zinc deficiency predisposes plants to infection. Soil temperatures of 28–32 °C are favorable. Under humid conditions at 22–25 °C sporangia form in 3 hours and a second generation appears after 9 hours. 12 hours of leaf wetness is required.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: An obligate biotroph. Sporangiophores are short and determinate, emerging from substomatal cavities. Sporangia are hyaline, ovoid to nearly cylindrical, operculate, **18.5–26 × 29–66.5 µm**, borne in groups of 2–6 with a distinct peduncle and smooth walls. Each contains 4–8 zoospores. Encysted zoospores are globose, 7.5–11 µm.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Oogonia are 33–44.5 µm in diameter, subglobose, thin-walled, hyaline to pale straw-colored. Oospores are **29.5–37 µm**, globose to subglobose, with a smooth, glossy wall 4 µm thick fused to the oogonial wall. Contents are hyaline with a distinct oil globule. More are formed at high temperatures above 28 °C.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Table 1: *S. rayssiae* var. *zeae* has short, hypha-like, determinate sporangiophores. Sporangia are 18.5–26 × 29–66.5 µm and **germinate by zoospores**. Oospores are brown, globose, 29.5–37 µm. In contrast, conidiophores of the four *Peronosclerospora* species are long (150–550 µm) and dichotomously branched, and conidia **germinate by a germ tube**. Sporangia of *S. macrospora* (crazy top) are lemon-shaped, 30–60 × 60–100 µm, and oospores are mainly in vascular bundles.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Small Grains manual datasheet, *P. philippinensis* (Table 1, citing White 1999) (CAPS-Pp-SG)

features.description: The CAPS-approved method is morphological identification. "No serological or molecular diagnostic methods are known" (at the time of writing). NPDN has produced a diagnostic standard operating procedure (SOP).
features.short_quote: "no known serological or molecular diagnostic methods"
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: *Sclerophthora* is likely a species complex, or many misidentifications occurred in the past through morphological identification. This study first clearly separated *Sclerophthora* and *Peronosclerospora* by molecular means.
features.source_name: Groben G. et al. 2026, Fungal Syst. Evol. 17:221–232 (CC BY 4.0) (Groben2026)

features.description: Crazy top (*S. macrospora*): phyllody, with the tassel turning into a leafy mass, and excessive tillering. Sorghum downy mildew (*P. sorghi*): chlorosis, frequent stunting, white streaks, narrow upright leaves and phyllody of the tassel. **None** of these symptoms is observed with brown stripe downy mildew. Var. *rayssiae* (barley downy mildew) is very similar but differs in host range.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

features.description: Physiological disorders (fertility, weather and so on) and other endemic downy mildews can also produce similar symptoms.
features.source_name: USDA CAPS Corn manual datasheet, *Sclerophthora rayssiae* var. *zeae* (CAPS-Sr)

source_conflicts: Scientific name: EPPO treats var. *zeae* as a synonym under *S. rayssiae*, CAPS uses var. *zeae*, and Groben 2026 uses *S. zeae*.
Streak color change: CAPS 'red to purple (some genotypes), then pale brown, burnt', Singh 'brown and burnt after necrosis'. The red-purple stage appears only in CAPS.
The streak width of 3–7 mm was confirmed only in CAPS.
Mixed terminology: the Key Diagnostics of CAPS-Sr uses 'conidiophores and conidia' (*Peronosclerospora* style), while the Pest Description of the same document uses 'sporangiophores and sporangia'.

Molecular diagnosis: CAPS says 'no known serological or molecular diagnostic methods' (at the time of writing); Groben 2026 provided the first molecular data from type specimens, but not a diagnostic protocol.
The full EPPO datasheet (morphology and symptom sections) could not be compared due to a server error.
diseases.photo_visible: Vein-bounded chlorotic streaks 3–7 mm wide only on leaves turning brown and burnt-looking, progressing from lower leaves, no leaf shredding or malformation, down on both surfaces on cool, humid mornings.
diseases.lab_required: Operculate sporangia (18.5–26 × 29–66.5 µm) and brown oospores in the mesophyll (microscopy), genus-level separation from *Peronosclerospora* (germination mode), molecular diagnosis (current availability Unconfirmed).

diseases.intro: No Korean source confirmed. No Korean occurrence data were found for MCMV, SCMV or MLN. Below are descriptions from an international organization (CIMMYT), a US state government (CDFA), reviews and original papers.

features.description: Early MLN symptoms: **mosaic and mottling**.
features.source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

features.description: **Necrosis starting at the leaf margins** appears together with mottling.
features.source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

features.description: **'Dead heart'** symptom (death of the growing point and young leaves).
features.source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

features.description: Husks dry early, and grain filling is poor or there is no grain set.
features.source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)

features.description: Three-column layout of the flyer: SCMV symptoms = 'mild mosaic and mottling'; MCMV symptoms = 'shortened internodes, severe chlorotic mottling'. Whether the second-row 'severe chlorosis and leaf necrosis' belongs to the MCMV or the MLN column is unclear from the layout (**interpret with caution**).
features.source_name: CIMMYT, "Disease Symptoms of Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN)" flyer (CIMMYT-Flyer)
features.location_in_source: p.1 photo descriptions (column headings SCMV / MCMV)

features.description: Common MLN symptoms: chlorotic spots intensify, growth is suppressed and plants yellow. Long yellow streaks wider than MSV streaks form. Leaves yellow and dry **from the outer margin toward the midrib**, and whole plants usually dry and die **from the top down**. Dead plants are **scattered** among healthy-looking plants.
features.short_quote: "higher intensity of chlorotic spots, stunted growth and yellowing"
features.source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

features.description: With late infection tassels fail to emerge and ears are poor: small and malformed, with few kernels or empty.
features.source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

features.description: Newly emerging leaves show marginal necrosis. Upper internodes shorten, and young leaves develop streaks, mottling, mosaic and narrow stripes. Plants are shorter, and distinct pale green-yellow mottling persists to the end of the season. Single infections can recover from mosaic, but in MLN the mottling persists.
features.source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

features.description: Plants infected with MCMV alone show **pale green mottling** alternating light and dark green.
features.source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

features.description: SCMV alone: mosaic with normal-green 'islands' embedded in a pale green or chlorotic background. It is most distinct on fast-growing young leaves and fades as leaves age.
features.source_name: Awata L.A.O. et al. 2019, J. Gen. Mol. Virol. 9(1) (PMC7753892) (Awata2019)

features.category: Symptoms - whole plant (MCMV alone vs MLN)
features.description: MCMV infection symptoms: chlorotic mottling, mosaic, chlorotic and necrotic streaks, leaf necrosis, stunting, poor ear development, malformed ears and early death. Severity depends on genotype, age at infection, environment, isolate and co-occurring viruses. MLN mixed infections are usually more severe than single infections, and early infection causes systemic necrosis, severe stunting, death and large yield losses.
features.source_name: CDFA California Pest Rating Proposal: Maize chlorotic mottle virus (comment period 2026-07-16 to 08-30) (CDFA-MCMV)

features.description: MCMV inoculation alone: **mild chlorotic mottling** on new leaves after 10 days (agro-inoculation) or 6 days (sap inoculation), with mild symptoms. MCMV+SCMV co-infection: **severe systemic necrosis** (CLND) of leaves and stems (figure 15 days after inoculation).
features.source_name: Wang Q. et al. 2017, Scientific Reports 7:39960 (PMC5216416) (Wang2017)

features.description: 1–9 scale for MCMV resistance evaluation: 6 = strong chlorotic mottling and marginal necrosis over the whole plant; 8 = excessive chlorotic mottling, leaf necrosis, dead heart, sometimes early death; 9 = necrosis of the whole plant, sometimes death. The final score is taken 40 days after the first inoculation.
features.growth_stage: Up to about 40 days after inoculation

features.description: MCMV or SCMV alone usually cause milder symptoms, and together they rapidly act synergistically. Plants are susceptible at **all growth stages** from seedling to maturity.

source_conflicts: Severity of single infection: CIMMYT and Wang 2017 say MCMV alone is 'mild', but CDFA says single infection can also cause necrosis, stunting, ear malformation and early death, attributing the difference to experimental conditions.
Whether the 'severe chlorosis and leaf necrosis' row on the CIMMYT flyer belongs to the MCMV or the MLN column is uncertain from the layout.
The SCMV particle length of 708 nm comes only from Awata 2019, and Wang 2017 does not give a length. Awata also gives the SCMV genome length inconsistently as 9,610 nt and 5–12 kb.
MCMV vectors: CIMMYT lists thrips and several beetles, while Awata's text ('the only vector is *F. williamsi*') and Table 2 (listing beetles) disagree.

Direction of progression: Awata 'from margin to midrib, from top to bottom of the plant', CIMMYT 'starting at the margin'. The description in the original Wangai 2012 report is Unconfirmed because the original was not viewed.
No primary source directly comparing MLN with drought or nitrogen deficiency was found.
diseases.photo_visible: Chlorotic mottling and mosaic on young leaves, necrosis starting at leaf margins, dead heart, early drying of husks, dead plants scattered among healthy plants.
diseases.lab_required: Detection of MCMV and the potyvirus separately (ImmunoStrip, DAS-ELISA, RT-PCR, NGS), confirmation of symptomless carriers, identification of vector species.
